title: Rewards and Inheritance
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Rewards and inheritance teaches that God graciously honors faithfulness and gives His people an eternal inheritance in Christ. These rewards are gifts of grace, not wages that earn salvation.
summary: Rewards and inheritance teaches that God graciously honors faithfulness and gives His people an eternal inheritance in Christ. These rewards are gifts of grace, not wages that earn salvation.
christFocus: Jesus Christ secures the believer’s inheritance and promises to reward faithful service. Every reward is received through Him and returned to His glory.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture speaks of reward without teaching salvation by works. Believers are saved by grace, yet God graciously honors faithfulness done through His grace.

The believer’s inheritance is kept by God. It is imperishable, undefiled, unfading, and secure in Christ.

Rewards show that the Lord sees what people often miss. Faithful service, endurance, sacrifice, and hidden obedience matter to Him.

This doctrine should produce gratitude rather than pride. Every faithful work is enabled by God, and every reward belongs to the grace of Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some believers fear that hidden faithfulness is meaningless because no one notices. Others serve for human applause. Scripture points both toward Christ’s evaluation and eternal inheritance.

This doctrine encourages perseverance. The Lord is not unjust to forget the labor of love done for His name.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Serve the Lord faithfully, not for human applause, but as one who will receive an inheritance from Him. Steward your gifts, endure quietly when needed, and let future reward strengthen present obedience.
